oneliner.t: Pelham Democrat and Spectrum Business account executive who served on the Pelham City Council from 2012 to 2025, the last years as council president, and lost the 2025 Pelham mayoral race.

upbringing.t: Few early-life details are documented in the sources reached. He has lived in Pelham since 2005 and says that from 2008 he pushed as a private citizen for a city library and recreation center before winning a council seat in 2012. In 2020 he was described as founder of Kats, Inc., a food-logistics company honored by Shelby County as a 2019 small business.

career.role: Pelham City Council member (Place 4 in 2020); council president in his final term
Candidate for Mayor of Pelham (lost to Rick Wash)

platform.t: Top priority: raising the minimum wage.
Cites rising living costs as a reason for running.
Cites the war in Iran as a reason for running.

promises.t: Work to raise the minimum wage (his stated top priority).

claims.claim: Served three terms on the Pelham City Council (elected 2012).

record.t: The Shelby County Reporter said in June 2020 that he had served two terms covering the prior eight years and was seeking re-election. BirminghamWatch reports he served until 2025.

claims.claim: Was the first Black person elected to the Pelham City Council (2012).

record.t: Both mentions trace to BirminghamWatch and likely to the candidate. No independent city or historical record was reached.

claims.claim: Served as council president from 2020 to 2025.

record.t: BirminghamWatch's news story says he was president for 'the last four years' of his service. That is broadly consistent but does not match 2020–2025 exactly, and no city minutes were reached.

claims.claim: Holds a business administration degree from Troy University.

record.t: Single candidate-supplied source; no registrar record reached.

claims.claim: Earned Advanced Certified Municipal Officer status from the Alabama League of Municipalities.

record.t: Single candidate-supplied source; League of Municipalities records not reached.

claims.claim: Nominated Public Servant of the Year three years in a row.

record.t: The profile does not name the awarding body; no record found.
A stated belief about competitiveness. For context, Palmer won 70.3% in 2024, and every listed forecaster rates AL-06 Safe/Solid R.

claims.claim: Sees an unprecedented opportunity in the historically Republican 6th District.

record.t: The checkable part holds. The seat has been held by Republicans continuously since 1993 (Bachus, then Palmer from 2015) and was also Republican from 1965 to 1983, with a Democrat holding it 1983–1993. Cook PVI is R+17, and Palmer won 70.3% in 2024.

claims.claim: Rising living costs and the war in Iran made him feel obligated to run.

record.t: The factual premise holds: U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran began Feb. 28, 2026, and the conflict was still ongoing as of July 2026 after a June ceasefire collapsed. The cost-of-living part was not rated because no 2026 BLS figures could be reached.

aipac_endorse.t: Not listed — he does not appear on Track AIPAC (as of 2026-10-08); AIPAC's endorsement page was not checked.

udp.note: Not listed on Track AIPAC; no UDP spending found in sources reached.

fec.history_note: First federal race; committee Friends to Elect Mercer (C00951533) registered May 24, 2026. FEC data runs through Jun 30, 2026. The Reflector reported $6,500 raised and $4,700 spent through Jul 22, so the pre-primary report was not yet in FEC summary data. 'Other receipts' of $2,358.96 is not itemized on the summary page. His 2025 Pelham mayoral campaign (a municipal race, not FEC) had raised $20,790.19 by June 2025 per 1819 News. Outside spending: none found.

note.t: No House candidate financial disclosure was located; the Clerk's search form could not be used. No net-worth or asset data.
Has lived in Pelham (Shelby County, in AL-06) since 2005.

checks.legal: Not done. CourtListener is blocked, Justia was not reached, Alacourt is paywalled, and no news search for lawsuits or charges was possible (search budget exhausted). Nothing turned up in the BirminghamWatch, Reflector, 1819 News or Shelby County Reporter coverage reviewed.
checks.foreign: No financial disclosure located; FARA blocked. Nothing found in news reviewed.
checks.claims: The mechanical sample could not be run: mauricemercer.com could not be fetched (tool permission not granted), and no ads were found. Fallback: his candidate profile on BirminghamWatch (candidate-supplied) plus statements quoted in Aug 2026 coverage. Seven claims; six are checkable bio facts, five of them unverifiable from independent records. Oct 8 pass: mauricemercer.com was still blocked. BirminghamWatch's profile (candidate-supplied, no issue statements) confirms that URL as his site. Re-read the Reflector, BirminghamWatch, 1819 News and Shelby County Reporter stories. His only reported policy statement is raising the minimum wage (a position). Added 2 claims, both true. Total: 9 claims, 3 rated true, 5 unverifiable, 1 opinion. Still short of 5 checkable verdicts.
checks.democracy: Reviewed his BirminghamWatch profile and coverage from the Reflector (2026-08-11), BirminghamWatch (2026-08-12), 1819 News (2025-06-25) and the Shelby County Reporter (2020-06-17). None contains a statement on the 2020 or 2024 results. His campaign site was unreachable, and new news searches could not be run.

research_notes: Ethics is marked 'na' because House Ethics covers only members; Alabama Ethics Commission filings for his municipal service were not checked. The 2025 mayoral loss is inferred from two sources: 1819 News reported a two-way race between Mercer and fellow councilman Rick Wash, and Wikipedia lists Wash as mayor from 2026. Vote totals were not found. The Kats, Inc. founder detail comes from 2020; his current job is given as Spectrum Business account executive. Same depth and source set as the other AL-06/AL-07 candidates; the search budget ran out mid-research, which limited all four files equally on courts and claims. WEB LIMITS (Oct 8, 2026 pass): the shared web-search budget was used up, and outbound connections to campaign sites, web.archive.org, census.gov, bls.gov, congress.gov and the House Clerk's disclosure search were blocked or refused. CLAIMS: fewer than 5 rated verdicts. The campaign site was never reached, so this is not a confirmed 'publishes fewer than 5' finding; checklist.claims stays 'news'. Wikipedia's Pelham article does not mention council history. The 'first Black council member' and 'president 2020–2025' claims need city records (pelhamalabama.gov minutes). DISCLOSURES: candidate financial disclosure not located; stays 'no'. DEMOCRACY: set to 'news'; no results statement found in coverage reviewed.
